Version 2.7.0 — much less data in the background.

• Checking for new messages in the background now uses far less data: the app holds the connection open longer instead of reconnecting constantly, and skips redundant lookups on secured chats.

• Roughly 50% less background data with the new Data saver off, and around 60% less with it on — on mobile data the saver also stops background update checks and eases off further when the connection drops.

• New setting in Settings → Background data: Automatic (saves only on mobile data), Always, or Never.

• Messages stay end-to-end encrypted; only the checking overhead shrinks, so nothing about delivery changes.

Version 2.6.1 — fixes and polish.

• The message input now grows smoothly as you add lines, and the chat above it slides up so the input bar never covers your last message.
• The keyboard now closes properly when you leave a conversation (instead of lingering outside incognito mode).
• More reliable Cloudflare connection and lower battery use after switching back to Tor.
• Small privacy and stability improvements.

Version 2.6.0 — choose how you connect.

• On first launch you can now pick how the app reaches the server: over Tor (recommended, maximum privacy) or directly via Cloudflare (faster and lighter on the battery).

• Messages stay end-to-end encrypted either way — the choice only affects network metadata like your IP.

• Change it anytime in Settings → Chat server.

Version 2.5.0 — accent-coloured chat bubbles and a tidier settings screen.

• Your sent messages now follow the accent colour you pick in Appearance, each accent a distinct light shade — so the choice finally shows in the chat.

• The app-lock delay is now a compact switch instead of a tall list.

• Settings cleanup — removed a few rarely-used options: copying the key to the clipboard, the file-size limit, and pausing update reminders.

• Removed the older, duplicate key verification; the security code from key rotation is the one to use.

Version 2.4.1 — a quick fix for the full-screen windows.

• The full-screen What's new and update windows can now be scrolled and their button tapped on every phone. On some phones the button did nothing and scrolling only half worked, depending on the phone — it was not a performance issue.

• The same fix applies to the lock screen, so unlocking always responds.

Version 2.4.0 — stronger privacy, safer pairing and lots of reliability fixes.

⚠️ For a NEW remote pairing, both phones should be on 2.4.0: the verification code (SAS) is now longer, so a new and an old phone would show codes that don’t line up. Existing chats keep working no matter which phone updates first.

• Hidden photo and file sizes — photos and files are padded before sending, so the server can’t tell how big they are (it already can’t see the content).

• Stronger verification code — the code you read aloud when pairing is longer and much harder to forge.

• Configurable auto-lock — Settings lets you pick how long after leaving the app it locks: immediately, 10s, 30s, 1min or 5min.

• Better full-screen photos — they open instantly, animate like the rest of the app, and no longer flash on screen before the app lock.

• Tighter block on key changes — if a verified contact’s security code changes, every way of sending (reactions, retry and delete-for-everyone too) pauses until you re-verify, not just the send button.

• Stronger backup password — backups now need at least 8 characters.

• Fewer lost messages — many fixes so a message can’t be silently dropped when a write fails, a failed reaction rolls back instead of looking sent, and more.

• Sturdier server and privacy — the relay resists flooding better, and bug reports no longer leak IP addresses or Tor identifiers.

• Assorted scroll and tap fixes across several screens.

Version 2.3.0 — formatting, reaction alerts and reliability. You can update one phone at a time.

• Text formatting — wrap text in *stars* for bold, _underscores_ for italics, ~tildes~ for strikethrough or `backticks` for monospace. The marks disappear and the styling shows; it’s still sent as plain text, so an older phone just sees the marks.

• Reaction alerts — when someone reacts to a message you sent, you get a notification showing which message they reacted to (long ones are shortened).

• Full-screen photos — tap a photo in a chat to open it full screen, then pinch to zoom and drag to pan.

• Incognito keyboard — the message box now asks your keyboard not to learn or cloud-sync what you type, so drafts of your messages don’t leak out of the app.

• Safer key changes — if a verified contact’s security code changes, sending pauses until you re-verify them or tap to continue anyway.

• Fewer lost messages — a message that reached the server but never got a delivery receipt is quietly sent again, so it’s less likely to get stuck on one tick.

• Faster reconnect — when the connection comes back (Wi-Fi to mobile data, or after a dropout), the app picks up messages right away instead of waiting.

• The app is now called CryptoChat, and updates keep working across the rename.

• What’s new now keeps the last few versions, so skipping an update no longer loses its notes.

Version 2.2.0 — edit and delete messages.

• Edit a message you sent — hold it, pick Edit, fix the text and send. It updates on the other phone too and is marked “edited”.

• Delete for everyone — hold your own message and pick Delete for everyone; it turns into a grey “Deleted” on both phones. Delete for me does the same only on this phone.

• Both phones need this version for edits and deletes to reach the other side; an older phone simply keeps the original.

• Scrolling fixes — reading older messages no longer jumps you back to the bottom when a new one arrives, and the jump-to-latest badge now shows the right count.

Version 2.1.1 — a quick fix on top of 2.1.0.

• Fixed a crash when scrolling up in a conversation. It could happen when messages weren’t in strict time order (a clock difference between the two phones, or a message that arrived late), and got more likely the longer the conversation.

All of 2.1.0 is included: day separators and a “New messages” line, tap a quote to jump to the original, a jump-to-latest button, drafts that survive a restart, contact verification with a security-code warning, invite-only pairing with QR, backup servers, and a connection diagnostics screen.

Version 2.1.0 — a big one, mostly around conversations, trust and reliability.

In conversations:
• Day separators (Today / Yesterday / date) and a “New messages” line above the first unread one.
• Tap a quoted message to jump to the original, which lights up briefly.
• A “jump to latest” button appears when you scroll up, with a count of new messages.
• Unsent text is kept as a draft — it survives leaving the conversation and restarting the app, and the contact list shows “Draft”.

Trust and security:
• You can now mark a contact as verified and it sticks. If their security code ever changes, the conversation warns you.
• Adding a contact is simpler: pairing is done by invite only, and the invite can be shown and scanned as a QR code.

Connection:
• You can set backup servers. When the main one is down, messages go out over a backup and are also picked up from there.
• A new “Connection diagnostics” screen in Settings shows how Tor is starting up and how the server is responding.

Fixes:
• Taps no longer get swallowed on slower phones — the reaction bar could stay invisible but still catch them.
• Deleting a contact now really erases everything belonging to them.
• Re-doing a key exchange now truly switches to the new key.
• Fewer lost messages when a backup server is involved.

Version 2.0.2 — a quick follow-up to 2.0.1.

• The app icon is now the right size (it was too large and filled the whole tile).

Also from 2.0.1: no silently dropped messages when saving fails, the lock covers the app instantly, and more reliable delivery around midnight.
